extracted.intended_audience: Researchers/authors preparing and submitting manuscripts to Mathematische Annalen (mathematicians submitting to this Springer journal)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for preparing and submitting original mathematics manuscripts to Mathematische Annalen, covering formatting, ethical responsibilities, data and authorship statements, figures/tables, supplementary material, and post-acceptance procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and simultaneous submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission implies the work described has not been published before and is not under consideration elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submission also implies publication has been approved by all co-authors and responsible authorities at the institute. Submitting the same manuscript simultaneously to multiple journals is prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissions for reused material
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must obtain permission for figures, tables, or text passages already published elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permissions must cover both print and online formats and evidence of permission must be included at submission; material received without permission evidence will be assumed original.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online submission procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts must be submitted via the 'Submit manuscript' hyperlink and all files uploaded as instructed on-screen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the on-screen submission workflow; supply all required files. Missing files may lead to non-consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of editable source files
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide all relevant editable source files at every submission and revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failing to submit a complete set of editable source files will result in the article not being considered for review. Manuscript text should be submitted in common word processing formats such as .docx or LaTeX.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title page contents
rubrics_metrics.description: The title page must contain specific bibliographic and contact information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include concise informative title; author names; affiliations (institution, department, city, state, country); corresponding author email; ORCID(s) if available. For unaffiliated authors provide city and country of residence only.

rubrics_metrics.name: ORCID recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: If available, include the 16-digit ORCID of the authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are recommended to use ORCID when submitting or can acquire an ORCID via the submission process.

rubrics_metrics.name: LLM / AI authorship policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Large Language Models (LLMs) do not satisfy authorship criteria and cannot be listed as authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of LLMs must be documented in Methods (or an alternative section). AI-assisted copy editing (readability/grammar/style fixes) need not be declared. Human accountability for the final text is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract length and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an abstract of 150 to 250 words without undefined abbreviations or unspecified references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For life science journals specific trial registration details are requested when applicable (not typically relevant for this mathematics journal).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statements and Declarations inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Include required statements under the heading 'Statements and Declarations' in the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declarations must cover Competing Interests and other relevant items; submissions missing relevant declarations will be returned as incomplete. Use and adapt sample wording as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematics Subject Classification (MSC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an appropriate number of MSC classification codes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MSC codes are used for indexing in Mathematical Reviews and Zentralblatt MATH; follow www.ams.org/msc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred manuscript format (LaTeX)
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts should be submitted in LaTeX and the Springer Nature LaTeX template is encouraged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submission should include original source (style files and figures) plus a PDF of compiled output. Word files are also accepted, but LaTeX is preferred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Text formatting and source inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide all relevant source files (including style files and figures) and a PDF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the submission includes everything necessary to compile the manuscript; include original source at every revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heading structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Use decimal system of headings with no more than three levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep heading depth to three levels to conform with journal style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abbreviation usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Define abbreviations at first mention and use consistently thereafter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid undefined abbreviations and ensure they are clear to readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Footnotes policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Footnotes may be used to give additional information but not to contain bibliographic details or only reference citations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Footnotes to text are numbered consecutively; footnotes to tables use superscript lower-case letters (or asterisks for significance). Always use footnotes instead of endnotes. Do not include figures/tables in footnotes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgments placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Place acknowledgments (people, grants, funds) in a separate section on the title page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write funding organization names in full.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical notation style
rubrics_metrics.description: Use standard mathematical notation conventions for font styles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Italic for single letters denoting constants/variables/unknowns; roman/upright for numerals/operators/punctuation and common functions (cos, det, e, exp, lim, log, max, min, sin, tan, d); bold for vectors/tensors/matrices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation style in text
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify reference citations by numbers in square brackets in the text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples provided show use like [3], [1-3, 7]. Maintain numbering and use in-text numeric citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference list content and numbering
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference list should include only works cited in the text and be numbered consecutively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include unpublished works or personal communications in the reference list; such items may be mentioned in text only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include DOIs in references
rubrics_metrics.description: If available, always include DOIs as full DOI links in the reference list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use full link format e.g. 'https://doi.org/abc' where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal name abbreviations
rubrics_metrics.description: Use standard journal name abbreviations according to the ISSN List of Title Word Abbreviations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If unsure, use the full journal title.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table numbering and captions
rubrics_metrics.description: Number tables using Arabic numerals and supply a caption explaining table components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite tables in text in consecutive numerical order. Identify previously published table material with a reference at the end of the table caption. Table footnotes use superscript lower-case letters or asterisks for significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic figure submission and file formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Supply all figures electronically and indicate the graphics program used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preferred formats: EPS for vector graphics, TIFF for halftones. MSOffice files are also acceptable. Name files like 'Fig1.eps'. Embed fonts in vector graphics containing fonts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Line art requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Line art should be black and white with legible lines and lettering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All lines should be at least 0.1 mm (0.3 pt) wide. Scanned line drawings/bitmap line drawings should have minimum resolution 1200 dpi. Embedded fonts required for vector graphics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Halftone (photograph) resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Halftone art (photographs/drawings with shading) must meet minimum resolution standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Halftones should have minimum resolution of 300 dpi. If magnification used, indicate scale bars within figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combination artwork resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Combination art (halftone + line art) must meet higher resolution standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combination artwork should have a minimum resolution of 600 dpi.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color art submission and print considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Color art is free online but ensure information is still visible in black and white print.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If print will be black and white, do not refer to color in captions. Submit color illustrations as RGB (8 bits per channel). Authors may be charged for color in print versions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure lettering and fonts
rubrics_metrics.description: Use sans serif fonts (Helvetica or Arial) for figure lettering and keep sizes consistent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for final-sized lettering about 2–3 mm (8–12 pt). Minimize variance of type size within an illustration; avoid outline/shading effects. Do not include titles or captions within illustrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure numbering and part labeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Number figures using Arabic numerals; denote figure parts by lowercase letters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite figures in text in consecutive numerical order. Continue numbering through appendices (do not use A1, A2 for appendix figures), except figures in online appendices/SI should be numbered separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure captions format
rubrics_metrics.description: Each figure must have a concise caption; captions go in the text file, not the figure file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Captions begin with the term 'Fig.' in bold followed by the figure number in bold. No punctuation after the number or at the end of the caption. Identify all elements found in the figure and cite previously published material at end of caption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure placement and sizing guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Place figures within the body of the text and size them to fit column width specifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If file size prevents embedding, submit large figures separately. Size for large journals: 84 mm (double-column) or 174 mm (single-column) wide, not higher than 234 mm; small journals: 119 mm wide, not higher than 195 mm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissions for previously published figures
rubrics_metrics.description: Obtain permissions for previously published figures; Springer cannot refund permission costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If electronic rights are not granted by other publishers, use alternative material. Provide permission evidence at submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure accessibility requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure figures are accessible to people with disabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide descriptive captions usable by text-to-speech or Braille. Use patterns in addition to/instead of color, and ensure figure lettering has contrast ratio at least 4.5:1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generative AI images policy for figures
rubrics_metrics.description: Adhere to Springer’s policy on generative AI images when including AI-generated images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the journal/publisher policy and ensure work follows described principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary Information file types and submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplementary Information (SI) may include multimedia and other files to be published online with the article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supply SI in standard file formats; include article title, journal name, author names and corresponding author contact in each file. Keep file sizes reasonable for download. Examples: videos (specific formats), PDFs for text, .csv or .xlsx for spreadsheets, specialized formats like .pdb, .nb, .tex also accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary material naming and numbering
rubrics_metrics.description: Name supplementary files consecutively and reference them from the text as 'Online Resource'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'ESM_3.mpg', 'ESM_4.pdf'. Cite them in-text similar to figures/tables: 'Online Resource 3'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Captions for supplementary materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide concise captions describing the content of each supplementary file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include captions in the manuscript text file rather than in the supplementary file itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing of supplementary files
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplementary files will be published as received without conversion, editing, or reformatting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure files are final and in appropriate formats prior to submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility for supplementary files
rubrics_metrics.description: Make supplementary files accessible to users with disabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure manuscript contains descriptive captions for each SI; video files should avoid flashing more than three times per second.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing services are optional
rubrics_metrics.description: Using professional editing or manuscript-preparation services is optional and not a requirement for publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Services include English language editing, formatting, figure preparation, translation. Using such services does not guarantee editorial acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical publication standards (COPE membership)
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal follows COPE guidelines and expects authors to uphold integrity of the scientific record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should refrain from misrepresenting results and follow good scientific practice; COPE procedures will be followed in cases of alleged misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data integrity and manipulation prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Results must be presented clearly, honestly, and without fabrication, falsification or inappropriate data manipulation (including image manipulation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should adhere to discipline-specific rules for acquiring/selecting/processing data and be prepared to provide raw data when requested, subject to privacy/confidentiality constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plagiarism and proper acknowledgement
rubrics_metrics.description: No data, text, or theories of others may be presented as the author's own. Proper acknowledgements and quotation marks for verbatim copying are required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The journal may use software to screen for plagiarism. Avoid text-recycling/self-plagiarism without transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid salami-slicing / duplicate publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not split a single study into several submissions to increase publication count.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concurrent or secondary publication can be justifiable in certain conditions (e.g., translations) but must meet transparency conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure and permissions for tools/questionnaires
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure permissions exist for use of software, questionnaires, surveys and scales used in the research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secure and be able to document appropriate permissions if required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate and balanced citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Research and non-research articles must cite appropriate and relevant literature to support claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excessive or coordinated self-citation is strongly discouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid defamatory or untrue statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should avoid untrue statements about entities or personal attacks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be careful in descriptions that could be construed as allegations about individuals or companies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual-use research identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Research that may be misapplied to threaten public health or security should be clearly identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: creating harmful biological agents, disruption of vaccine immunity, weaponization of technology. Authors must flag such risks in the manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct and stable authorship at submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are strongly advised to ensure author group, corresponding author, and author order are correct at submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adding/deleting authors during revision is generally not permitted and cannot be made after acceptance. Changes require explanation and may be approved at Editor-in-Chief discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to supply documentation/data on request
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should be prepared to send relevant documentation or data to verify results when requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This may include raw data, samples, records; sensitive/confidential data is excluded. Failure to provide such material may affect the manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions and corrections for misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: If misconduct is found, the journal/publisher will investigate and may reject, publish corrections, expressions of concern, or retract articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outcomes depend on severity; retracted articles remain on platform watermarked ‘retracted’ with explanatory note. The author’s institution may be informed and notices may be added to bibliographic records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to correct fundamental errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must correct significant errors or inaccuracies discovered after publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact the journal to explain the impact; actions may include correction or retraction, and retraction notes should provide transparency about affected parts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer suggestions and exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may suggest suitable reviewers and/or request exclusion of certain individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested reviewers must be independent and not connected to the work; provide institutional email addresses or other verifiable identifiers (homepage, publication record, researcher ID). The journal may or may not use suggestions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competing interests disclosure timing and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose financial or non-financial interests directly or indirectly related to the work, covering interests within the last 3 years of beginning the work; older interests should be disclosed if relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosing interests enables readers to judge potential bias; disclosure is not an implication of impropriety. Examples of interests to disclose include funding, employment, stocks, consulting fees, patents, editorial positions, advisory roles, mentoring relations. Specific wording examples are provided and primary research and review articles require disclosure statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary of declarations placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Summarize funding and competing interests in a 'Declarations' section before the reference list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other declarations include Ethics approval, Consent, Data/Material/Code availability, and Authors' contribution statements. Funding information must also be provided in the peer review system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of competing interest statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Use provided example phrasings for 'no funding', 'funding received', 'no competing interests', and for listing specific financial/non-financial interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Customize sample statements as appropriate; when all authors have the same/no conflicts one blanket statement suffices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship criteria (recommended)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommended authorship criteria adapted from ICMJE: substantial contribution, drafting/revision, approval, and accountability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically: (1) substantial contributions to conception/design/acquisition/analysis/creation of software; (2) drafted or revised critically for important intellectual content; (3) approved final version; (4) agree to be accountable for all aspects ensuring questions about accuracy/integrity are investigated/resolved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosures and declarations to include
rubrics_metrics.description: Include sources of funding, financial/non-financial interests, ethics approvals, informed consent, and animal welfare statements where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inclusion depends on article scope; authors must consider public health implications and include needed disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data transparency requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must ensure data and materials (including code) support published claims and comply with field standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journals may have individual policies on sharing research data; follow disciplinary norms and the journal’s Research Data Policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corresponding author responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: One author acts as Corresponding Author on behalf of all co-authors and must ensure accuracy, communication, and inclusion of declarations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responsibilities include ensuring all listed authors approved the manuscript and order, managing communications between journal and co-authors, providing transparency on reuse of material, and ensuring disclosures from all authors are included. Managing communication may be delegated to a Contact/Submitting Author but the Corresponding Author must be clearly indicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author contribution statements recommended (CRediT)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include contribution statements specifying each author's contributions when possible; examples and CRediT taxonomy are provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide free-text statements or CRediT roles such as Conceptualization, Methodology, Formal analysis, Writing - original draft, Writing - review & editing, Funding acquisition, Resources, Supervision. For review articles, describe idea, literature search, data analysis, drafting/revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graduate student thesis authorship guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: For articles based primarily on a student's dissertation/thesis, the student is usually listed as principal author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to guidance such as 'A Graduate Student’s Guide to Determining Authorship Credit and Authorship Order' for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affiliation and address policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary affiliation should be the institution where the majority of work was done; current addresses may be additionally stated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses will not be updated after publication. For unaffiliated authors, only city and country are recorded; email not captured unless requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policies on changes to authorship
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes to authorship, corresponding author, or author sequence are not accepted after acceptance and generally discouraged during revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adding/deleting authors at revision is generally not permitted but may be warranted in specific cases; reasons must be explained and approval during revision is at the Editor-in-Chief’s discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author name publication accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Author names will be published exactly as they appear on the accepted submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure names are present, correctly spelled, and affiliations current before acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deceased or incapacitated author inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: If a co-author dies or becomes incapacitated and co-authors wish to include them, approval from a legal representative (e.g., direct relative) should be obtained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain appropriate approval before including deceased/incapacitated authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship disputes handling
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal will not adjudicate authorship disputes; authors must resolve disputes themselves or involve their institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If authors cannot resolve disputes, the journal may withdraw a manuscript or involve the authors’ institution for published papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-acceptance production and communication
rubrics_metrics.description: After acceptance the article goes to Production for typesetting and authors will receive emails to confirm affiliation, publishing model, rights/payment, and proofs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One email includes affiliation/rights/publishing model choices and payment; a second email links to proofs. Authors must act on proofs promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article publishing agreement and copyright
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors will either grant an exclusive licence to the Publisher or transfer copyright depending on ownership/policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open Choice articles retain copyright with authors and are published under a Creative Commons license; see journal's 'How to publish with us' guide for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offprints and color illustration charges
rubrics_metrics.description: Offprints can be ordered by corresponding author; online color is free but print color may incur extra costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors choosing color in print are expected to contribute towards extra costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofreading scope and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Proofs are for checking typesetting/conversion errors and completeness; substantial changes to content are not allowed without Editor approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantial changes (new results, corrected values, title, authorship) require Editor approval. After online publication further changes can only be made via Erratum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online First publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles are published online after corrected proofs are received and this is the official first citable publication (with DOI).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After print release the paper can also be cited by issue/page numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open Choice (hybrid open access) option
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may choose Open Choice to publish open access in Springer Nature hybrid journals for an APC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: APCs vary by journal; benefits include increased accessibility, higher visibility and easier compliance with funder mandates. Details on fees, funding, and licenses are available on the journal's Open Access pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research data policy: Data Availability Statement requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All original research must include a Data Availability Statement explaining how to access supporting data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statement should explain access to datasets analysed or generated, including links to publicly archived datasets, or, if not possible, describe access conditions and reuse restrictions. Authors are encouraged to consider the minimal dataset necessary to interpret and replicate findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research data repositories encouragement
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are strongly encouraged to deposit supporting data in publicly available repositories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use discipline-specific repositories where available. For some data types deposition in specific repositories may be mandatory. Authors should ensure they have rights to share data and are encouraged to use open licences permitting reuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data citation best practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Cite publicly available data supporting conclusions, including persistent identifiers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data citations should include persistent identifiers (DOI) and follow DataCite minimum information (Dataset Creator, Title, Publisher [repository], Year, Identifier) and follow journal reference style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and peer review anonymity guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: When double-anonymous peer review is used and authors provide reviewers with data, authorship in the data should also be anonymised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use repositories that can help anonymise authorship or create masked links to datasets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for research data policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors who need help with data sharing or repository selection can consult the Research Data Helpdesk and FAQ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resources are provided for guidance on policy interpretation and practical steps to share data.
